title: SystemSoftware
description: A third-party or platform software product, such as an operating system, language runtime, database engine, message broker, cache server or container runtime, that is installed or run on a node or device to host, execute or store other software and data. It is configured and versioned by the team, but its code is not written by them. Use Node instead when the element is the computational host itself (VM, container instance, Kubernetes cluster) that runs software, rather than the software product running on it. Use Artifact instead when the element is the deployable file or package (a container image tag, installer, binary, config file) rather than the running platform software it delivers. Use TechnologyService instead when the element is the capability consumed through an interface (e.g. a managed database or queueing offered by a cloud provider) rather than the specific software product that provides it. Use Device instead when the element is physical hardware rather than software installed on it.

documentation.description: Free-text description of the software product: its name, version or edition, and its role in the deployment. Set it whenever the product, version or notable configuration choices (e.g. clustering mode, persistence settings) are not evident from the element name.

softwareType.description: Platform software category, per ArchiMate 3.2 SystemSoftware element.

x-dr-evidence: A docker-compose service or Kubernetes container spec whose image is a vendor platform product, e.g. image: postgres:15, redis:7-alpine, rabbitmq:3-management, nginx:1.25
A runtime or OS pin such as a Dockerfile 'FROM node:20-alpine' or 'FROM ubuntu:22.04', an .nvmrc/.python-version file, or an 'engines' field in package.json
A connection URL, driver dependency or Helm chart dependency naming an engine, e.g. DATABASE_URL=postgres://..., spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers, or a bitnami/kafka chart in Chart.yaml
